concepts.term: Power transfer in a circuit device
concepts.def: The power of a circuit device is the rate at which it transfers energy, that is the energy it transfers each second. A device with a larger power transfers more energy in the same time.
The power transferred by a circuit device is found by multiplying the potential difference across the device by the current through it: power = potential difference x current.
The symbol form of power = potential difference x current, where P is power in watts, V is potential difference in volts and I is current in amperes.

The power transferred by a circuit device can also be found from the current through it and its resistance: power = (current)^2 x resistance. The current is squared, so the power is very sensitive to the current.
The symbol form of power = (current)^2 x resistance, where P is power in watts, I is current in amperes and R is resistance in ohms.
Power, P, is measured in watts, W. One watt is an energy transfer of one joule each second, so a 60 W lamp transfers 60 J of energy every second it is switched on.
Potential difference, V, is measured in volts, V. One volt is one joule of energy transferred per coulomb of charge that flows.
Current, I, is measured in amperes, A, and amp is acceptable for ampere. A current of one ampere is a charge flow of one coulomb each second.
Resistance, R, is measured in ohms. Resistance opposes the flow of charge in a circuit, and for a given current a larger resistance means a larger power transfer.
An everyday electrical appliance such as a kettle, a lamp or a food mixer is designed to bring about a particular energy transfer when a current flows through it.
The amount of energy an appliance transfers depends on two things: how long the appliance is switched on for, and the power of the appliance.
In appliances such as a food mixer, a drill or a washing machine, energy is transferred electrically from batteries or the ac mains to the kinetic energy of an electric motor.
In appliances such as a kettle, a toaster or an iron, energy is transferred electrically from the ac mains to a heating device, raising the temperature of water, food or metal.
Portable appliances are usually supplied by batteries, which provide a direct current. Appliances plugged into sockets are supplied by the ac mains.
Work is done when charge flows in a circuit. The energy transferred by that work comes from the store associated with the source, such as the chemical store of a battery.
The energy transferred by electrical work can be calculated from the power of the device and the time for which it operates: energy transferred = power x time.
The symbol form of energy transferred = power x time, where E is energy transferred in joules, P is power in watts and t is time in seconds.

concepts.term: energy transferred = charge flow x potential difference
concepts.def: The energy transferred by electrical work can also be calculated from the charge that flows and the potential difference it moves through: energy transferred = charge flow x potential difference.
The symbol form of energy transferred = charge flow x potential difference, where E is energy transferred in joules, Q is charge flow in coulombs and V is potential difference in volts.
Energy transferred, E, is measured in joules, J. One joule is transferred when a power of one watt operates for one second.
Time, t, is measured in seconds, s, in E = P t. Times given in minutes or hours must be converted to seconds before the equation is used.
Charge flow, Q, is measured in coulombs, C. A charge flow of one coulomb passes when a current of one ampere flows for one second.

concepts.term: Energy transferred over a given time
concepts.def: Because energy transferred = power x time, the power of a device is the energy it transfers divided by the time in seconds. Two devices can transfer the same energy at different powers if they run for different times.

The power rating printed on an appliance is the power it transfers when working normally. A higher power rating means a faster change in the stored energy of the appliance and its surroundings while it is in use.
The National Grid is a system of cables and transformers that links power stations to consumers such as homes, schools and factories.
A step-up transformer increases the potential difference from the power station to the transmission cables, which reduces the current in those cables for the same power.
A step-down transformer decreases the potential difference, to a much lower value, for domestic use, so that mains electricity reaches consumers at a safe potential difference.
Transmitting at a high potential difference means a low current in the cables. Because the power wasted by heating the cables is given by P = I^2 R, a lower current wastes much less energy.

mcqs.q: Two devices are connected across the same 12 V supply. Device X draws a current of 2.0 A and device Y draws a current of 0.50 A. Which statement about the two devices is correct?
options: Device X has the greater power, so it transfers energy for a longer period.
Device X has the greater power, so it transfers more energy each second.
The two have equal power, because the pd across each of them is the same.
Device Y has the greater power, as a smaller current is much safer.
mcqs.explain: P = V I, and X has the larger current at the same pd, so X transfers energy at the greater rate.

mcqs.q: A potential difference of 12 V drives a current of 0.25 A through a circuit device. What is the power transfer in the device?
mcqs.explain: P = V I = 12 x 0.25 = 3.0 W, with pd in volts and current in amperes giving power in watts.

mcqs.q: In the equation P = V I, what does each symbol stand for and in which unit is it measured?
options: P is power in W, V is pd in V and I is current in A.
P is power in W, V is the pd in A and I is the current in V.
P is the pd in V, V is power in W and I is current in A.
P is power in J, V is pd in V, and I is current in A.
mcqs.explain: These are the quantities and the units the specification gives for P = V I.

mcqs.q: A current of 0.60 A flows through a resistor of resistance 12 ohms. What is the power transferred in the resistor?
The current through a fixed resistor is doubled. What happens to the power transferred in the resistor?
options: The power becomes four times greater, because P = I^2 R squares the current.
The power becomes two times greater, as current and power are proportional.
The power is unchanged, because the resistance itself has not altered.
The power becomes half as large, because the current is being shared.
mcqs.explain: Substituting 2I gives (2I)^2 R = 4 I^2 R, so the power is multiplied by four.

mcqs.q: Which line gives the units the specification uses for power and for potential difference?
options: Power is measured in joules, J, and the pd is measured in volts, V.
Power is measured in watts, W, and pd is measured in amperes.
Power is measured in watts, W, and pd is measured in ohms.
Power is measured in watts, W, and pd is measured in volts, V.
mcqs.explain: The specification gives power, P, in watts, W, and potential difference, V, in volts, V.

mcqs.q: Which line gives the units the specification uses for current and for resistance?
options: Current is measured in amperes, A, and resistance in volts, V.
Current is measured in amperes, A, and resistance in ohms.
Current is measured in coulombs, C, and resistance in ohms.
Current is measured in amps, A, and resistance in watts.
mcqs.explain: The specification gives current, I, in amperes, A, with amp acceptable for ampere, and resistance, R, in ohms.

mcqs.q: An electric kettle is plugged into the mains and switched on. Which statement best describes why the kettle is built as it is?
options: It is designed to create new energy from the mains supply that it uses.
It is designed to store the electrical energy the mains delivers.
It is designed to bring about a particular energy transfer.
It is designed to use up the current flowing in from the mains.
mcqs.explain: Everyday electrical appliances are designed to bring about energy transfers, here to the thermal store of the water.

mcqs.q: A 2000 W kettle is switched on for 2 minutes. A 100 W lamp is switched on for 1 hour. Which transfers more energy?
options: The kettle, because it has the higher power rating of the two appliances.
The kettle, because its rating already gives the energy it transfers.
They are equal, because both of them are supplied by the same mains.
The lamp, because energy transferred depends on the time as well as the power.
mcqs.explain: E = P t: 100 W for 3600 s is 360 000 J, while 2000 W for 120 s is only 240 000 J.

mcqs.q: A hairdryer has a power of 1500 W. It is switched on for 4 minutes. How much energy does it transfer?
A food mixer is plugged into a wall socket and switched on. How is energy transferred while it is in use?
options: Electrically from the ac mains to the thermal store of the mixer motor.
Electrically from batteries to the kinetic energy of the motor.
Electrically from the ac mains to the kinetic energy of the motor.
From the mains supply to the chemical store of the mixer.
mcqs.explain: A mixer is designed to turn a blade, so the useful transfer is to the kinetic energy of an electric motor.

mcqs.q: A cordless drill and an electric kettle are both in use. Which statement about their supplies is correct?
options: The drill is supplied by batteries and the kettle by the ac mains.
The drill is supplied by the ac mains and the kettle by its batteries.
Both are supplied by the ac mains, as both contain a heating device.
Both are supplied by batteries which are recharged after use.
mcqs.explain: Portable appliances are supplied by batteries; appliances plugged into sockets use the ac mains.

mcqs.q: A lamp is connected to a cell and lights up. Which statement about work in this circuit is correct?
options: No work is done, because nothing in the circuit can be seen moving.
No work is done, because the current leaving equals that entering.
Work is done, because charge is flowing through the lamp.
Work is done only while the lamp is warming up to temperature.
mcqs.explain: Work is done when charge flows in a circuit, and that work transfers energy to the lamp.

mcqs.q: Which equation does the specification give for the energy transferred by electrical work in terms of power?
options: energy transferred = power x time, with the time measured in seconds.
energy transferred = power / time, with the time given in seconds.
energy transferred = power x time, with time given in minutes.
energy transferred = power + time, with the time in seconds.
mcqs.explain: This is the equation the specification gives for the energy transferred by electrical work, E = P t.

mcqs.q: A kettle has a power of 2000 W. It is switched on for 90 s. How much energy does it transfer?
mcqs.explain: E = P t = 2000 x 90 = 180 000 J, with the power in watts and the time in seconds.

mcqs.q: A lamp has a power of 60 W. It transfers 5400 J of energy. For how long was it switched on?
options: 1.5 min
mcqs.explain: Rearranging E = P t gives t = E / P = 5400 / 60 = 90 s.

mcqs.q: Which line gives the equation for energy transferred in terms of charge flow, with the correct units?
options: E = Q V, where Q is charge flow in amperes and V is the pd in volts.
E = Q V, where Q is charge flow in coulombs and V is pd in volts.
E = Q / V, where Q is charge flow in coulombs and V is the pd.
E = I V, where I is the current in A and V is pd in volts.
mcqs.explain: The specification gives energy transferred = charge flow x potential difference, E = Q V.

mcqs.q: A motor connected to a 12 V supply takes a current of 5.0 A for 60 s. How much energy is transferred?
An electric motor transfers 5400 J of energy when the potential difference across it is 18 V. What charge flowed through it?
mcqs.explain: Rearranging E = Q V gives Q = E / V = 5400 / 18 = 300 C.

mcqs.q: Which units does the specification give for energy transferred and for time in E = P t?
options: Energy in joules, J, and time in minutes, min.
Energy in watts, W, and time in seconds, s.
Energy in joules, J, and time in seconds, s.
Energy is in joules, J, and time is in hours, h.
mcqs.explain: The specification gives energy transferred, E, in joules, J, and time, t, in seconds, s.

mcqs.q: Which units does the specification give for charge flow and for potential difference in E = Q V?
options: Charge flow in coulombs, C, and pd in volts, V.
Charge flow in amperes, A, and the pd in volts, V.
Charge flow in coulombs, C, and the pd in watts, W.
Charge flow in joules, J, and the pd in volts, V.
mcqs.explain: The specification gives charge flow, Q, in coulombs, C, and potential difference, V, in volts, V.

mcqs.q: A circuit device is switched on. Which statement about the power of the device is correct?
options: Its power is the pd across it added to the current through it, giving watts.
Its power is the total energy that it transfers, whatever the time taken.
Its power is the pd across it times the current, and the energy given each second.
Its power is the current through it divided by the pd that is across it.
mcqs.explain: P = V I gives the power from the circuit quantities, and E = P t shows the same power as the energy transferred per second.

mcqs.q: Heater X transfers 30 000 J in 60 s. Heater Y transfers 48 000 J in 120 s. Which heater has the greater power?
options: Heater Y, because it transfers more energy altogether than heater X does.
Heater Y, because it was switched on for the longer period of time.
They have equal power, since both transfer their energy steadily.
Heater X, because it transfers 500 J each second and Y transfers 400 J.
mcqs.explain: P = E / t: X gives 30 000 / 60 = 500 W and Y gives 48 000 / 120 = 400 W.

mcqs.q: A cook boils the same pan of water on a 2400 W hob and then on a 900 W hob. Which statement is correct?
options: The 2400 W hob transfers exactly the same energy over the same period of time.
The 2400 W hob raises the temperature of the water faster than the 900 W hob.
The 900 W hob raises the temperature of the water more quickly than the 2400 W hob.
The 2400 W hob transfers just 2400 J in total before it is switched off.
mcqs.explain: A higher power rating means the thermal store of the water is filled at a greater rate.

mcqs.q: What is the National Grid?
options: A system of cables alone that links all of the power stations to consumers.
A system of cables and transformers linking power stations to consumers.
A system of power stations that generates all of the energy consumers use.
A system of transformers that increases the energy that is sent to consumers.
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's description of the National Grid.

mcqs.q: Electrical power is transferred from a power station to homes. In which order are transformers used along the way?
options: Step-down transformers first, then step-up transformers near the consumers.
Step-up transformers at both ends, to keep the pd high all the way.
Step-up transformers first, then step-down transformers near consumers.
Step-down transformers at both ends of the transmission cables.
mcqs.explain: Step-up transformers raise the pd for the transmission cables; step-down transformers lower it to a much lower value for domestic use.

mcqs.q: Why is the National Grid an efficient way to transfer energy from power stations to consumers?
options: A high pd gives a low current, so less energy is wasted heating the cables.
A high pd makes the energy travel along the transmission cables much faster.
A high pd lowers the resistance of the long cables used in the National Grid.
A high pd increases the power that the power station is able to supply.
mcqs.explain: For a given power, raising the pd lowers the current, and the power wasted is I^2 R.

mcqs.q: A transmission cable of resistance 5.0 ohms carries a current of 1000 A. What power is wasted in heating the cable?
mcqs.explain: P = I^2 R = 1000^2 x 5.0 = 5 000 000 W wasted in heating the cable.
